survey: A blue plastic sports water bottle, floating at an angle against a yellow sunburst. Main parts: (1) The body is a waisted bottle with oval grip indents on both sides and a recessed round base, seen from below at a three-quarter angle. Its shape is symmetrical and consistent. (2) A ridged screw cap sits on the threaded neck, with a darker collar ring where cap and body meet. (3) A short spout nozzle rises from the centre of the cap, with its opening facing the camera. It has no dust cover, which is a simplification. (4) A carry loop is pinned to the right side of the cap with a round rivet. It arcs up and over, and its other end comes back down to meet the spout itself, at the right side of the nozzle rim, not the cap. The bottle floats as a hero object on an abstract background, so it needs no support. The water drops are surface detail, not invented parts.

errors.where: Carry loop, upper end where it meets the spout (top right of the bottle)
errors.what: The loop is anchored by a rivet on the cap at one end only. The other end melts into the side of the spout's rim and has no real attachment. On a real sports bottle the carry loop is fixed to the cap at both ends, or to a hinged lid. It is never joined to the nozzle, because the nozzle has to pull up and push down to open and close. As drawn, the strap would block the spout, and its anchor point is unclear.

fix: Sports water bottle with a carry loop attached to the screw cap at both ends: both ends of the loop are fixed to opposite sides of the cap with matching round rivets. The loop arcs above the cap and stays clear of the spout. The spout nozzle stands free in the centre of the cap, with nothing touching it.
